name: Gangtok
description: Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim, perched at around 1,650 m in the Eastern Himalayas, offering clear-day views of Kangchenjunga and a mix of Buddhist monasteries, colonial-era charm, and mountain trekking. It suits travelers who enjoy cool weather, mountain scenery, and cultural depth, though the town itself can feel crowded and commercialized in peak season. Permits are required for many excursions, and weather is highly unpredictable — cloud cover can obscure mountain views for days at a stretch.
nearest_railhead: New Jalpaiguri (NJP), approximately 124 km from Gangtok
nearest_airport: Pakyong Airport (PYG), approximately 30 km from Gangtok; Bagdogra Airport (IXB) is a more reliable alternative at approximately 124 km

attractions.name: Rumtek Monastery
attractions.description: The largest monastery in Sikkim and the seat of the Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism, housing important relics and the Golden Stupa. The complex is visually impressive and spiritually significant, though visitor access to inner chambers can be restricted.

attractions.name: Tashi Viewpoint
attractions.description: A popular hilltop viewpoint north of Gangtok that offers wide views of the Kangchenjunga range and the Singtam valley on clear days. The best views depend entirely on weather — mist and clouds are common, and early morning visits give the best chance of clear skies.

attractions.name: MG Marg (Mahatma Gandhi Marg)
attractions.description: The pedestrianized main street of Gangtok lined with shops, restaurants, and cafes — this is where the town comes alive in the evenings. It is more of a social and food hub than a sightseeing attraction, but useful for orientation and getting a feel for local life.

attractions.name: Enchey Monastery
attractions.description: A 200-year-old Nyingma monastery perched on a ridge above Gangtok town, dedicated to Kanchenjunga. It is quieter than Rumtek and easier to visit independently, with decent views of the surrounding hills and a peaceful atmosphere on weekday mornings.

attractions.name: Do-Drul Chorten Stupa
attractions.description: One of the most important stupas in Sikkim, built in 1945, surrounded by 108 prayer wheels and mani walls. It is compact and easy to walk around, and works well as a short stop combined with other central Gangtok sights.

attractions.name: Namgyal Institute of Tibetology
attractions.description: A serious research institution and museum housing an extensive collection of Tibetan and Sikkimese manuscripts, thangkas, masks, and ritual objects — one of the best of its kind outside Tibet. The building itself is architecturally notable; the collection rewards slow, careful visitors rather than those passing through quickly.

attractions.name: Nathu La Pass
attractions.description: A high-altitude mountain pass at 4,310 m on the Indo-China border, one of the three open trading border posts between India and China. The drive from Gangtok is dramatic but the pass itself is heavily militarized and visited under strict permit conditions — altitude sickness is a real risk, and the experience is more about the journey and bragging rights than the destination.

attractions.name: Tsomgo Lake (Changu Lake)
attractions.description: A glacial lake at 3,753 m, roughly 40 km east of Gangtok and often paired with Nathu La on the same day trip. The lake is scenic in good weather but tends to be very crowded with tour groups; the surrounding landscape can be bleak outside of spring (April–May) when rhododendrons bloom.

attractions.name: Hanuman Tok
attractions.description: A hilltop Hindu temple at about 2,200 m maintained by the Indian Army, with genuinely good views over Gangtok and the Kangchenjunga range on clear mornings. It is less crowded than the main viewpoints and has a calm atmosphere — a worthwhile short detour for both views and the temple itself.

attractions.name: Pangolakha Wildlife Sanctuary (Birding Trails)
attractions.description: A genuinely lesser-visited sanctuary near the Bhutan border, reached via Rongli or Aritar, known among serious birders for blood pheasants, satyr tragopan, and Himalayan monal. Facilities are minimal and access requires planning, but for wildlife and nature photography enthusiasts this is one of East Sikkim's best-kept secrets.
